text: A collector lease does not by itself prevent an expired owner from continuing work. Process pauses can produce overlapping leaders; Kubernetes client-go explicitly disclaims fencing. (high confidence)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: When client-go ReleaseOnCancel is enabled, all lease-guarded work must finish before cancelling the election context; its source warns that otherwise two processes may act on the critical path. For a graceful collector handoff, drain or terminate guarded work before releasing ownership. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: Recommended handoff invariant: make event processing durable before advancing the recoverable replay checkpoint, and make replayed processing idempotent. This applies Amazon’s durability-before-completion rule to Salesforce’s process-then-commit protocol; it is a design inference, not a Salesforce transaction guarantee. (medium confidence)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: The redlease implementation warns that asynchronous Redis replication can lose an acknowledged token increment during failover. Its token monotonicity is therefore not a failover-safe guarantee; use a linearizable token authority when that guarantee is required. (low confidence)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: To resume a normal Salesforce subscription after handoff, use CUSTOM with the replay ID of the last keepalive or processed event, whichever arrived last; store the opaque ID as bytes. (low confidence)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: Kleppmann’s fencing pattern assigns an increasing token on each lock acquisition and requires the storage service to reject writes with older tokens. A collector design can apply this pattern to prevent a resumed former owner from overwriting a newer owner’s state; a lease check in the process alone cannot close the pause-before-write race. (high confidence)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: Salesforce documents a normal 72-hour event-retention window, but rare org moves can reset retained streams and make events inaccessible. Replay catch-up requires retained history; EARLIEST retrieves retained events and cannot restore already-purged history. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: ManagedSubscribe resumes from the last successfully committed Replay ID when the client reconnects with the same subscription ID. Processing precedes committing, and CommitReplayResponse reports success or failure; sending a commit request alone does not establish a persisted checkpoint. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: Salesforce documents a managed subscription as unique per client and says it cannot be shared with other clients in the same org. Server-side replay storage therefore must not be assumed to provide a general multi-client leader-election or fencing protocol. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: Do not use an administrative ManagedEventSubscription STOP/RUN cycle as a cursor-preserving handoff: STOP deletes the previously committed Replay ID, and a later restart begins from defaultReplay rather than the former checkpoint. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: With Subscribe, the successor can create a new RPC using CUSTOM and the stored replay_id to resume after that position. Preserve replay IDs as opaque bytes rather than calculating the next ID. Replay options are read from the first FetchRequest; changing position requires a new Subscribe call. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Collector leader leases and subscriber handoff recovery

text: For an idle Subscribe stream, Salesforce recommends saving the replay_id from empty keepalive responses for resubscription. As a collector safety inference, advance that checkpoint only after all earlier delivered work is durable, so a crash does not skip pending work. (medium confidence)
